items.passage: The town of Fernwick sat where two rivers met. Each spring the northern river flooded first, carrying meltwater down from the hills, and a week later the southern river rose with rain from the plains. The townspeople built their market on the low ridge between the two rivers, so that it stayed dry while the fields on either side flooded in turn.
items.stem: According to the passage, why was the market built on the ridge?
options: So it stayed dry when the rivers flooded
So it was close to the hills
So traders could cross both rivers
